2026-08-14T03:51:13.9981305Z ## MCP Servers Mounted as Shell CLI Commands
2026-08-14T03:51:13.9981541Z 
2026-08-14T03:51:13.9981771Z The following servers are available as CLI commands on `PATH`:
2026-08-14T03:51:13.9982249Z 
2026-08-14T03:51:13.9982535Z - `safeoutputs` — run `safeoutputs --help` to see available tools
2026-08-14T03:51:13.9982847Z 
2026-08-14T03:51:13.9983967Z > **IMPORTANT**: For `safeoutputs` and `mcpscripts`, **always use the CLI commands** listed above instead of the equivalent MCP tools. The CLI wrappers are the preferred interface — do **not** call their MCP tools directly even though they may appear in your tool list.
2026-08-14T03:51:13.9985042Z >
2026-08-14T03:51:13.9986608Z > For `safeoutputs`, treat every successful command as a real write-intent declaration. Do **not** use `safeoutputs` for exploratory probing, auth checks, placeholder payloads, repeated "try again" variants, or manual runtime experiments. When you need a safe-output, emit the final intended call once. If you are not ready to perform the real action, use `noop` or `report_incomplete` instead.
2026-08-14T03:51:13.9988141Z >
2026-08-14T03:51:13.9988665Z > For all other servers listed here, they are **only** available as CLI commands and are **not** available as MCP tools.
2026-08-14T03:51:13.9989138Z 
2026-08-14T03:51:13.9989254Z ### How to Use
2026-08-14T03:51:13.9989404Z 
2026-08-14T03:51:13.9989895Z Each server is a standalone executable on your `PATH`. Invoke it from bash like any other shell command:
2026-08-14T03:51:13.9990343Z 
2026-08-14T03:51:13.9990446Z ```bash
2026-08-14T03:51:13.9990796Z # Call a tool — pass arguments as --name value pairs
2026-08-14T03:51:13.9991268Z <server-name> <tool-name> --param1 value1 --param2 value2
2026-08-14T03:51:13.9991638Z ```
2026-08-14T03:51:13.9991770Z 
2026-08-14T03:51:13.9992129Z **Example** — using the `playwright` CLI:
2026-08-14T03:51:13.9992577Z ```bash
2026-08-14T03:51:13.9992931Z playwright --help                                  # list all browser tools
2026-08-14T03:51:13.9993454Z playwright browser_navigate --url https://example.com
2026-08-14T03:51:13.9993998Z playwright browser_snapshot                        # capture page accessibility tree
2026-08-14T03:51:13.9994451Z ```
2026-08-14T03:51:13.9994583Z 
2026-08-14T03:51:13.9995031Z **Example** — using the `safeoutputs` CLI (safe outputs) when you are ready to emit the final real action:
2026-08-14T03:51:13.9995563Z ```bash
2026-08-14T03:51:13.9995928Z safeoutputs add_comment --issue_number 42 --body "Analysis complete"
2026-08-14T03:51:13.9996343Z ```
2026-08-14T03:51:13.9996476Z 
2026-08-14T03:51:13.9996698Z **Example** — using the `mcpscripts` CLI (mcp-scripts):
2026-08-14T03:51:13.9997061Z ```bash
2026-08-14T03:51:13.9997405Z mcpscripts --help                                  # list all script tools
2026-08-14T03:51:13.9997955Z mcpscripts mcpscripts-gh --args "pr list --repo owner/repo --limit 5"
2026-08-14T03:51:13.9998390Z ```
2026-08-14T03:51:13.9998522Z 
2026-08-14T03:51:13.9998711Z ### Passing Multiple or Complex Arguments (Preferred)
2026-08-14T03:51:13.9998971Z 
2026-08-14T03:51:13.9999941Z **Preferred approach for any tool call with multiple or complex arguments**: supply a JSON object on stdin using `.` as the sentinel. The bridge parses stdin as the argument object, preserving all native types (numbers, booleans, arrays) without shell-quoting issues.
2026-08-14T03:51:14.0000948Z 
2026-08-14T03:51:14.0001056Z ```bash
2026-08-14T03:51:14.0001356Z # Full argument payload as JSON via printf pipe
2026-08-14T03:51:14.0014299Z printf '{"issue_number":42,"body":"### Title\n\nBody paragraph one.\n\nBody paragraph two."}' \
2026-08-14T03:51:14.0014983Z   | safeoutputs add_comment .
2026-08-14T03:51:14.0015220Z 
2026-08-14T03:51:14.0015660Z # Works with any tool — just match the parameter names from <server> <tool> --help
2026-08-14T03:51:14.0016425Z printf '{"title":"Fix: something","body":"Details here","labels":["bug","priority-high"]}' \
2026-08-14T03:51:14.0017020Z   | safeoutputs create_issue .
2026-08-14T03:51:14.0017331Z ```
2026-08-14T03:51:14.0017472Z 
2026-08-14T03:51:14.0018067Z **When pipes are blocked by the bash security policy**, write the payload to a file first and use **file redirection** with the `.` sentinel instead:
2026-08-14T03:51:14.0018725Z 
2026-08-14T03:51:14.0018833Z ```bash
2026-08-14T03:51:14.0019321Z # Step 1 — write the JSON payload to a file using the Write tool or a bash heredoc
2026-08-14T03:51:14.0019954Z # Step 2 — redirect the file into the CLI command using '<'
2026-08-14T03:51:14.0020460Z safeoutputs create_pull_request . < /tmp/payload.json
2026-08-14T03:51:14.0020761Z 
2026-08-14T03:51:14.0021066Z # This is equivalent to piping but does not require a separate command before '|'
2026-08-14T03:51:14.0021633Z safeoutputs add_comment . < /tmp/comment.json
2026-08-14T03:51:14.0022250Z ```
2026-08-14T03:51:14.0022395Z 
2026-08-14T03:51:14.0022548Z > **Why prefer JSON payload mode?**
2026-08-14T03:51:14.0023158Z > - Single operation for any number of arguments — no repeated `--key value` flags
2026-08-14T03:51:14.0023872Z > - Native types (integers, booleans, arrays) are preserved exactly as specified
2026-08-14T03:51:14.0024586Z > - No shell quoting or escaping needed for newlines, quotes, or special characters
2026-08-14T03:51:14.0025326Z > - Agents can construct the payload as a structured object before emitting the command
2026-08-14T03:51:14.0026180Z > - File redirection (`< file`) works even when pipes (`|`) are restricted
2026-08-14T03:51:14.0026569Z 
2026-08-14T03:51:14.0026680Z ### Notes
2026-08-14T03:51:14.0026828Z 
2026-08-14T03:51:14.0027314Z - **Prefer JSON payload mode** (`. < file` or `printf '{...}' | server tool .`) for any call with multiple arguments or complex values
2026-08-14T03:51:14.0028370Z - All parameters can also be passed as `--name value` pairs; boolean flags can be set with `--flag` (no value) to mean `true`
2026-08-14T03:51:14.0029391Z - Use `.` as the only argument to parse stdin as a JSON object (all parameters supplied at once)
2026-08-14T03:51:14.0030313Z - Parameter names with hyphens or underscores are interchangeable (e.g. `issue-number` and `issue_number` both work)
2026-08-14T03:51:14.0031191Z - Output is printed to stdout; errors are printed to stderr with a non-zero exit code
2026-08-14T03:51:14.0032537Z - Run the CLI commands inside a `bash` tool call — they are shell executables, not MCP tools
2026-08-14T03:51:14.0033264Z - These CLI commands are read-only and cannot be modified by the agent
2026-08-14T03:51:14.0033765Z </mcp-clis>
2026-08-14T03:51:14.0034089Z <github-context>

2026-08-14T03:51:14.0043709Z # hn-daily-digest
2026-08-14T03:51:14.0043889Z 
2026-08-14T03:51:14.0044003Z ## Instructions
2026-08-14T03:51:14.0044165Z 
2026-08-14T03:51:14.0044452Z Create a daily digest workflow for professional developers, referencing
2026-08-14T03:51:14.0045095Z relevant top Hacker News stories on technology that can be used today
2026-08-14T03:51:14.0045724Z by large companies. Every weekday, fetch the top 30 stories from the
2026-08-14T03:51:14.0046378Z Hacker News API (https://hacker-news.firebaseio.com/v0/topstories.json),
2026-08-14T03:51:14.0046999Z filter to stories with a score above 100 that are about software
2026-08-14T03:51:14.0047569Z engineering, cloud infrastructure, AI/ML, developer tooling, or
2026-08-14T03:51:14.0048182Z distributed systems. For each qualifying story include: the title, the
2026-08-14T03:51:14.0048803Z URL, the score, the number of comments, and a one-sentence summary of
2026-08-14T03:51:14.0049392Z why it is relevant to enterprise developers. Create a GitHub issue
2026-08-14T03:51:14.0050026Z titled "HN Digest – <date>" with the results formatted as a Markdown
